---
title: iCite
description: NIH iCite's monthly snapshot, every PubMed record with its citation metrics and the full citation graph.
---

[iCite](https://icite.od.nih.gov) (NIH Office of Portfolio Analysis) publishes
a complete database snapshot monthly on
[Figshare](https://nih.figshare.com/collections/4586573): one row per PMID
with the paper's identifiers, the influence metrics (Relative Citation Ratio,
NIH percentile, citation counts), the translation scores and the `cited_by`
and `references` PMID lists. The release lands the latest snapshot whole and
derives what a paper *is* (`annotation.icite__publication`), how it is cited as
of the snapshot (`annotation.icite__metrics`) and the graph itself
(`annotation.icite__citation`, one row per citing and cited pair). The
snapshot label (`2026-08`) is the version.

## Licence and citation

CC BY 4.0. Cite the snapshot by its Figshare DOI and
[Hutchins et al.](https://icite.od.nih.gov/about).

## Join keys

- `pmid` joins `annotation.pubmed__article`, `annotation.ncbi__gene_pubmed.pubmed_id` and `annotation.pubtator3__mention.pmid`.
- "Who cites X" is `WHERE cited_pmid = X` on `annotation.icite__citation`; the table is sharded by `cited_pmid`.
- `citing_pmid` is always an iCite record; `cited_pmid` is not (some edges cite a paper iCite has no record of).

## Good to know

- `raw.metadata` is the older 17-column export of the same snapshot, kept with its columns unchanged; `raw.icite__metadata` is the typed, complete one.
- Only the latest snapshot is in raw; earlier snapshots stay citable on Figshare.
